facts.text: The end-to-end latency budget lists every delay between an object appearing and the machine standing still, with a time allowance for each delay.
facts.quote: The end-to-end latency budget is the list of every delay between an object appearing and the machine standing still, with a time allowance for each.

facts.text: The end-to-end latency chain proceeds through sensing, detection and confirmation (usually over several consecutive frames), risk determination and action selection, network transmission of the brake command, brake dead time, brake-force build-up, and deceleration to a stop.
facts.quote: the software decides it is real, usually after seeing it in several consecutive frames (detection and confirmation)

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 describes the collision-system distance chain as detection, determination, action, machine stopping and a safe distance.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-3 describes the same chain as the parts of its "collision-system distance", detection, determination, action, machine stopping and a safe distance

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 requires the system manufacturer to communicate the typical delays in the collision system.
facts.quote: requires the system manufacturer to communicate the typical delays in the system [Chapters 3, 8]

facts.text: The object-detection standard ISO 16001 allows at most 300 ms for detection.
facts.quote: The object-detection standard ISO 16001 allows at most 300 ms for detection [Chapter 3].

facts.text: A road study reported about 170 ms of sensing plus 50 ms of detection error for an automated brake, compared with about 700 ms for a human driver.
facts.quote: A road study reported about 170 ms of sensing plus 50 ms of detection error for an automated brake, against about 700 ms for a human driver [Chapter 8].

facts.text: The booklet's brake response reference figures range from under 0.3 s to 2.5 s depending on the machine; its latency diagram labels published brake dead-time values as 0.3 s to 2.5 s by machine.
facts.quote: Brake response figures run from under 0.3 s to 2.5 s depending on the machine [Chapter 8].

facts.text: A realistic end-to-end latency chain spends roughly one second before full deceleration.
facts.quote: A realistic chain therefore spends roughly one second before full deceleration

facts.text: At 15 km/h, each second of delay corresponds to 4.2 m of travel.
facts.quote: at 15 km/h each second is 4.2 m of travel.

facts.text: One road round robin reported 0.4 s for brake-force build-up to full force.
facts.quote: Build-up to full force (0.4 s in one road round robin)

facts.text: The latency-chain diagram calculates physical stopping distance as speed squared divided by twice deceleration, corrected for grade and surface, and ends with the machine stopped and residual safe distance remaining.
facts.quote: Physical stopping: v squared over 2a, corrected for grade and surface

facts.text: The real values for the object-to-standstill latency chain must be measured on each machine rather than assumed from the booklet's quoted figures.
facts.quote: the time figures are those the booklet quotes, and the real values must be measured on each machine [Chapter 8].

facts.text: The end-to-end latency budget connects the sensor, software and brake teams: each team owns one segment, and the sum of the segments sets the required detection range.
facts.quote: The budget connects the sensor team, the software team and the brake team: each owns one segment, and the sum sets the required detection range.

facts.text: The program needs a physical end-to-end latency test that injects a known object event and time-stamps every stage from detection to measurable deceleration.
facts.quote: an end-to-end latency test, injecting a known object event and time-stamping every stage from detection to measurable deceleration, among the physical tests the program needs

facts.text: If perception delays consume the end-to-end latency budget, no brake model can recover the lost margin.
facts.quote: if perception delays eat the budget, no brake model can recover the lost margin [Chapter 8].
